component.name: EloraNotes
component.summary: A calm, minimalistic Markdown notes app

description.p: EloraNotes is a quiet, keyboard-friendly home for Markdown notes: folders, tags, wiki links and backlinks, a command palette, split editing with a live preview, and a soft glow highlight for the text that matters.

The folder menu on a note now lists the connected server under "Shared libraries": picking it moves the note into the shared library with its body, folder, tags, pin and icon, and the local file goes once the server has it. A shared note offers "Copy to this computer" instead. The server installer, run on a machine that already has a server, now asks whether to update it, uninstall it and keep the notes, uninstall it and delete them, or cancel.

With a shared note open, New (and the daily-note, template and wiki-link actions) now creates the note in the server's library instead of on your own disk: it joins the same folder, keeps the tag you are filtering by, and appears on everyone's sidebar straight away. The server writes it as an ordinary Markdown file with the folder, tags and body the client sent.

The server installer works on systems with a read-only /etc/systemd/system, such as NixOS: it registers a per-user service, keeps the notes in ~/.local/share/elora-server, turns on lingering so it still starts at boot, and prints the systemctl --user commands that manage it. A certificate from an earlier interrupted install is carried over with any notes, so the code clients confirm does not change.

The server installer creates the service group before the service user, so it no longer stops with "chown: invalid group" on systems where useradd does not make a group of its own, and an install left over from an earlier release is moved onto that group. The settings and key are readable only by the service user.

The server installer now downloads to a temporary folder before installing, so a read-only /usr/local or a full disk gets a clear message instead of a failed transfer, falls back to /opt/elora-server when /usr/local/bin cannot be written, and checks that the binary it installed actually runs. Settings are written without relying on sudo being present, and the network download reports the reason when it cannot complete.

Shared notes. One machine runs the EloraNotes server, which keeps the notes as plain Markdown files and serves them over TLS with a certificate each client pins on the first connection. Everyone who connects sees the server's notes in the sidebar under its name and edits them together: text merges as it is typed, each person's caret carries their name and colour, and a note somebody has open shows a dot on its card. Usernames come from the account each person is logged into, and the library structure (titles, folders, tags, pins, trash) travels with the text.

Installers for the server are included with this release for Linux and Windows; they ask for the server name, port and password, start it at boot and open the port in the firewall. The app gains a Shared library section in Settings.

The seam between the note list and the editor is a single soft divider now. It had been painted underneath the sidebar, so what showed there was the note list's scroll bar, drawn in the text colour; scroll bars rest faint and out of the way.

The divider beside the note list is softer and sits between even margins instead of leaving a wide empty band, and a window too narrow for two columns shows the editor alone rather than two cramped panes. The README screenshot shows the current look.

The Matugen theme works in the Flatpak: the sandbox now includes ~/.config/elora read-only, and the app looks for the generated colours there when its own config folder (the sandbox's private one) has none.

The Flatpak now includes the home Documents folder by name, because the XDG documents directory points at nothing on systems without a user-dirs file, which left the app with an empty, temporary home instead of the notes in Documents/EloraNotes.

The AppImage no longer carries its own copy of the Wayland client library: the graphics driver has to use the host's, so shipping one made the image fail to start on hosts whose driver expects a newer copy.

Installing a newer Flatpak bundle now replaces the copy the launcher runs, so the version installed is the version that starts, and the AppImage bundles the Wayland and keyboard libraries it needs instead of assuming the host provides them.
The Flatpak now updates itself like every other build, and Settings gained an Updates section that checks on demand and installs the result.
The colour controls in the formatting bar move as one group instead of splitting across rows at narrow widths, and closing the sidebar no longer leaves the note centred in a narrow column.
The sidebar's Notes, Pinned and Trash sections share one row again, with Trash reduced to its glyph.
Notes and settings now live in Documents/EloraNotes on every platform, which the Flatpak shares with other installs instead of keeping a private copy.
Packaging for every platform: AppImage, Flatpak, a Windows setup wizard, a macOS app bundle and portable builds, plus an in-app updater that understands each one.
